name: diagram
description: Interactive Mermaid diagrams and Apache ECharts charts beside VS Code chat: ask @diagram to draw, chart CSV, JSON or command output, and edit diagrams in Markdown.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Charts of a shell command's output and chart options with JavaScript code need a trusted workspace. Reading workspace and data files, and opening a diagram's file links, ask for confirmation first.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Charts of a shell command's output are not available in virtual workspaces.

chatParticipants.name: diagram
chatParticipants.description: Draw, change and explain diagrams and charts

commands.name: new
commands.description: Start a new diagram or chart instead of changing the current one

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Explain the current diagram or chart, or the selected parts

disambiguation.description: The user wants to draw, visualize, update or explain a diagram, such as a flowchart, sequence diagram, class diagram, state machine, entity relationship diagram, architecture overview, mind map, timeline or Gantt chart.
examples: Draw a sequence diagram of the login flow
Visualize the class hierarchy in this file
Make a flowchart of this algorithm
Add error handling to the diagram

disambiguation.description: The user wants to visualize data as a chart, such as a pie chart, bar chart, line chart, scatter plot, treemap, sankey, heatmap, radar chart, box plot, gauge or funnel, with the data given inline, in a file or as the output of a shell command.
examples: Render this data as a pie chart
Bar chart of the lines of code per folder
Plot the CSV file as a line chart
Show the disk usage of these directories as a pie chart
Treemap of the file sizes under src

languageModelTools.name: diagram_render
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show a Mermaid diagram or an ECharts chart in an interactive panel
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Show a Mermaid 12 diagram (flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, Gantt, mind map, architecture-beta, etc.) or an Apache ECharts 6 option (no maps) in the panel beside chat, replacing the current one. Users can select its items and send follow-ups. Returns the diagram type, or the render error to fix. To chart a file, command output or table, use diagram_chart.

source.description: Complete Mermaid source, or an ECharts option as JSON or as a JavaScript object literal with callbacks (formatter, renderItem, symbolSize, etc.); prefer templates such as "{b}: {c}" for plain formatters. Omit click directives, HTML, colors, backgrounds and fonts: the panel applies the theme and sizing.

language.description: Defaults to "echarts" for a source starting with "{", else "mermaid".

title.description: Short title shown in the panel.

clickPrompt.description: Chat request sent on the user's behalf when they click a node or chart item, with {label} replaced by its label, e.g. "Explain {label} in more detail". For explorable overviews.

links.description: Mermaid node ids mapped to code locations, absolute or relative to the first workspace folder, with optional lines: {"parse": "src/parser.ts#L42", "check": "src/checker.ts#L10-L30", "cli": "src/cli.ts"}. Clicking a linked node opens its location. Link only code you have read.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_chart
languageModelTools.userDescription: Chart data given inline, in a file or as a command's output
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Chart tabular data with Apache ECharts in the panel beside chat, replacing the current diagram. Give exactly one of "data" (inline), "file" or "command" (its standard output), e.g. a treemap of `du -ah src`. Infers columns and reports how it read the data. For full control of the option or callbacks such as renderItem, use diagram_render.

type.description: horizontalBar suits long labels; scatter compares the first two value columns; treemap/sunburst nest paths or label columns and sum children; sankey connects source/target columns or labels to a node per value column; heatmap pivots two label columns or uses value columns as columns; radar has an axis per value column; boxplot shows each group's spread; gauge shows one value; funnel orders stages by value. Histogram counts raw numeric samples in bins; select one value column and omit labelColumn, aggregate, sort and limit.

title.description: Short title shown in the panel.

data.description: Inline data: CSV, TSV, JSON (an array of objects or arrays, an object mapping names to numbers, or JSON Lines), a Markdown table or whitespace-separated columns.

file.description: Data file path, absolute or relative to the first workspace folder.

command.description: Shell command whose standard output is the data, run with /bin/sh (cmd.exe on Windows) in the first workspace folder, or the home directory without one, once the user confirms it.

format.description: "auto" (default) detects the format, including Markdown tables and JSON Lines; "json" reads JSON or JSON Lines.

labelColumn.description: Label column by header or generated name, e.g. "Column 2"; defaults to the first text column naming each row. Multiple names, outermost first, define treemap/sunburst levels, sankey stages (source, target), heatmap rows/columns, or the categories of a bar, line or area chart and a series per label of the second, for rows such as month,region,sales. Treemap, sunburst and sankey also split paths such as "src/webview/main.ts" into levels. ISO dates ("2026-01-02", "2026-01-02T14:30:00Z", "2026-01") give bar, line, area and scatter charts a time axis; other dates and plain years stay labels.

valueColumns.description: Value columns, one series each, or the first alone with a series per label. Defaults to numeric columns, excluding identifiers (id, rank, pid, etc.) and units differing from the first. Pie, doughnut, treemap, sunburst, gauge and funnel use only the first, scatter the first two (x, y); boxplot uses its raw numbers.

max.description: The top of a gauge's scale, or of every radar axis, in input units (bytes for sizes, seconds for durations). Inferred when left out.

aggregate.description: Combine rows sharing the same label or labels. "count" counts rows without a value column, e.g. one row per commit or log entry. Grouping precedes "sort" and "limit"; sort descending to keep the largest groups. Omit for boxplot, which summarizes raw groups itself.

sort.description: Sorts the rows by the first value column, or by their total in stacked charts, after grouping.

limit.description: Keep the first rows after sorting. Pie/doughnut exclude nonpositive values and combine omitted positive rows as "Other".

options.description: Merge an ECharts option: objects merge, null removes a setting, other values replace it. A "series" object applies to every series; an array of objects merges element by element, e.g. {"series": [{"label": {"show": false}}]}. Omit colors, backgrounds and fonts. JSON only; for callbacks use diagram_render with a JavaScript option.

clickPrompt.description: Chat request sent on the user's behalf when they click a chart item, with {label} replaced by its name, e.g. "Which files make {label} so large?".

bins.description: Histogram bins, of equal width; by default about √n bins of a round width (1, 2 or 5 × 10^n, at least 1 for whole numbers).

facetColumn.description: Split a Cartesian chart or histogram into one panel per distinct value of this column (at most 12 panels). Filtering happens first; aggregation, sorting and limits apply inside each panel. The facet column is excluded from automatic label/value inference.

facetColumns.description: Facet panels per row; automatic by default.

facetScales.description: Whether facet panels share axis ranges (default) or fit each its own.

filters.description: Keep rows matching ALL predicates before faceting, aggregation, binning, sorting or limits. Compare parsed cells: eq/neq use exact value and type (null matches missing cells); lt/lte/gt/gte require numeric cells and a number value; contains is case-sensitive text matching. Use input units: bytes for sizes, seconds for durations. An empty array clears filters.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_getState
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read the diagram shown in the diagram panel, with your edits and selection
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read the panel's current diagram or chart: source, revision, chart parameters, code links, render error, user edits, marks, selected items, and the ids of selectable edges, sequence messages and same-named chart items. Use before changing a diagram you have not seen, or when the user refers to "this", "these" or the selection.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_pickNodes
languageModelTools.userDescription: Ask you to select nodes, relationships or chart items in the diagram panel
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Ask the user a question and wait until they click their answer in the current diagram or chart, e.g. "Which step is failing?". Returns the picked labels and ids, with endpoints for edges and sequence messages, or why nothing was picked.

prompt.description: One short question shown above the diagram.

multiple.description: Let the user pick several items and confirm with Done. Defaults to false: the first click answers.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_annotate
languageModelTools.userDescription: Mark nodes, edges, sequence messages or chart items without drawing again
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Mark items of the current diagram or chart for a walkthrough, a problem or a path, without redrawing it. Each call replaces the previous marks, caption and fading; omit marks to clear them. Marks are not part of the source and clear when a new diagram is drawn. Returns which ids were marked and which are unknown.

id.description: Exact Mermaid node id, edge:/message: relationship id from diagram_getState, or chart item name. Chart items that share a name need the ids diagram_getState lists for them.

mark.description: "current" (default) for the step being explained, "problem" for a failure, "good" for something working or a recommended path, "info" for a pointer.

note.description: Short note shown above the diagram after the item's label, e.g. "times out after 30 s".

marks.description: Omit or pass [] to clear the marks.

caption.description: One line shown above the diagram, only for context the marks and labels do not show, e.g. "Step 2 of 3: the request is retried here".

dim.description: Fade unmarked items. Defaults to false.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_findFiles
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find files in all workspace folders by glob. Returns one path per line, usable as diagram_readFile's file and in code links. Honors files.exclude and search.exclude, and skips .git and node_modules.

glob.description: Glob relative to each workspace folder, e.g. "**/*.ts" or "src/**". Defaults to "**/*".

languageModelTools.name: diagram_searchText
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search workspace text files, including unsaved editor changes, for a literal string. Returns matching lines with their numbers, grouped by file path. Scans at most 1000 files and 16 MiB per call; narrow the glob when it reports incomplete results.

query.description: Literal text on one line, not a regular expression.

glob.description: Glob relative to each workspace folder, e.g. "**/*.ts" or "src/**". Defaults to "**/*".

languageModelTools.name: diagram_readFile
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read lines from a workspace file
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read numbered lines from a text file in an open workspace folder, including unsaved editor changes. Use the line numbers in code links.

file.description: Path as diagram_findFiles and diagram_searchText return it: relative to the first workspace folder, or absolute.

endLine.description: Inclusive; defaults to startLine + 199. Reads at most 500 lines.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_inspectData
languageModelTools.userDescription: Inspect columns and sample rows from the current chart or another data source
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Report a data source's columns, inferred types, row count and sample rows, without drawing anything. Omit the source to inspect the current chart's loaded data; otherwise give exactly one of data, file or command, which diagram_chart reads again when charting it.

data.description: Inline data: CSV, TSV, JSON (an array of objects or arrays, an object mapping names to numbers, or JSON Lines), a Markdown table or whitespace-separated columns.

file.description: Data file path, absolute or relative to the first workspace folder.

command.description: Shell command whose standard output is the data, run with /bin/sh (cmd.exe on Windows) in the first workspace folder, or the home directory without one, once the user confirms it.

format.description: "auto" (default) detects the format, including Markdown tables and JSON Lines; "json" reads JSON or JSON Lines.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_updateChart
languageModelTools.userDescription: Change the current chart's settings without reloading its data
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Change the current chart made by diagram_chart, reusing its loaded data without rereading files or rerunning commands. Settings mean the same as in diagram_chart; omitted ones are kept and null clears one. Keeps supported manual styling, and refuses changes that would lose unsupported manual source edits. To change the data source, use diagram_chart.

revision.description: Revision from diagram_getState; the update is refused if the chart has changed since.

diagram.codeLens.enabled.markdownDescription: Show an **Open in Diagram** action above every `mermaid` and `echarts` code block in a Markdown file, which opens the diagram in the panel. The **Diagram: Open Diagram at Cursor** command opens one without it.

scripts.package: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.mjs --production
